note: credentials and revocations signed by ca2a_runtime; headers are regtest difficulty

vectors.description: the operator never logs the delegator's revocation; two trusted witnesses acknowledged it and the acknowledgements were anchored before the block the responder says it had seen, so the execution is after a published revocation

the same refusal, and the operator signs a checkpoint whose as_of is past the time of the block max_merge_blocks after the witnessing, without carrying the revocation: the witnesses' and the operator's signatures show it
the operator does carry the witnessed revocation: no finding, and its log seq is reported
the threshold is two; one acknowledgement does not publish anything
a second acknowledgement from a key the relying party does not trust
three acknowledgements, all from the same witness, are one witness
a trust configuration listing the operator as a witness is refused
one of the two acknowledgements is for a different revocation and is not counted
an acknowledgement made for another log is not reused for this one

an acknowledgement's anchor is moved to a later block it is not in: the proof fails there, so only one anchor counts and the restriction has no upper bound; its two signatures still make it unresolved
an acknowledgement names a block the view does not hold: it gives no lower bound, but its anchor still shows the witness had signed by 96
the responder names block 95, older than the witnessing; it cannot be shown to have executed after the revocation, nor before it: order_unresolved, not within
the revocation reaches the witnesses only after the receipt was anchored, and is dated after the execution: it does not judge that execution
the same, but dated before the execution: cA2A's audit sees it, the blocks say it was published late, so late_revocation_only
the operator never logs the issuer's single-use limit; witnessed before both executions, the second use exceeds it
a witnessed limit signed by the leaf's subject is accepted by the lane and limits nothing
a credential use sent to the witnesses is rejected; uses and receipts need the operator's sequence
the leaf's own subject revokes it through the witnesses; cA2A gives it no authority
witnessed records but no witnesses in the trust configuration: each is rejected and the rest settles
witnesses without a threshold is a malformed trust configuration
acknowledgements anchored in the last block of the view have fewer confirmations than required
a witnessed revocation dated hours after its witnessing block is kept, flagged, and in force by block order; cA2A's audit by issued_at is reported beside it
the same revocation witnessed twice; the earlier publication height is the one used
a witnessed single-use limit whose order against the second execution cannot be fixed by blocks
an acknowledgement's seen block is changed after the witness signed: its signature fails
one acknowledgement in each of two records for the same revocation: together they reach the threshold, published at the later of the two

each witness signed once after block 95 (anchored at 100) and again after 98 (anchored at 99); publication is bounded by 99 above and 95 below, so against a receipt anchored at 97 the order is unresolved, not after
a checkpoint whose as_of equals the time of the block max_merge_blocks after the witnessing must carry the revocation; one second earlier it need not
the same checkpoint with as_of one second before that block's time: no finding
a checkpoint signed before the revocation existed and anchored again after the delay: its as_of is before the due block's time, so no finding; the receipt's order is unresolved
three honest witnesses; the third's acknowledgement is anchored too shallow to count upward, but it signed after block 95, so the revocation may have been public before the receipt: unresolved
two witnesses signed but nothing is anchored: the restriction exists with no upper bound, so it is unresolved against this receipt and no omission can be charged to the operator
the same acknowledgement bytes repeated are checked once; a copy with a different anchor is checked on its own, and here its anchor fails
the witnesses' own unanchored copies come before the calendar's anchored copies of the same acknowledgements: both are checked, the restriction is published at 96 and the omission is reported
two acknowledgements whose signature is a list or an object are rejected by name and the rest settles
both witnesses name a block below the view (an older lower bound, or a reorg): no lower bound, but their anchors still show they had signed by 96, which is before the receipt's seen block

the bundle carries the re-anchored checkpoint and, under extra_anchors, its first anchor at 97: the receipt existed by 97, the revocation was witnessed after 99, so the order is after and the receipt is within; without the first anchor it would be unresolved
the view ends before the due block: the omission check is reported as not possible, not as clean
